h1: What distillery consultancy covers, from still to bottle
title: What Distillery Consultancy Covers | Craft Beer School
desc: What a distillery consultant covers from still to bottle: planning, equipment, mash, distillation, cuts, maturation, quality and licensing for new distillers.
teaser: A still is simple to buy and hard to run well. Most of the value in a distillery sits in the decisions around it.
standfirst: Distillery consultancy runs from the plan on paper to the spirit in the bottle. This guide sets out the parts of that path so you can decide where you need help.
sections:
A distillery is built around a product. A neutral spirit, a gin, a malt whisky and a rum need different raw materials, different equipment and different times to market. Decide the product first.

Spirits that mature tie up cash for years. Gin and other unaged spirits can sell within weeks of distilling. Many new distilleries plan an unaged spirit first to bring in money while the aged product rests. Our guide on what goes into a project report shows how to model that cash gap.

Choices include pot stills, column stills and hybrids, plus mashing and fermentation vessels, condensers, spirit receivers and storage. The right choice follows the product. A pot still keeps more character. A column still gives a lighter, cleaner spirit.

Layout matters for safety as well as flow. Ethanol vapour is flammable, so spirit rooms need correct ventilation, electrical equipment and fire protection. Rules on this differ by place, so involve the competent authority and a safety engineer early.

The spirit starts at the mash. Raw material, milling, conversion of starch to sugar and yeast choice set the flavour you can distil later. A clean, controlled fermentation gives the distiller something good to work with.

On the still, the distiller separates heads, hearts and tails. These cuts decide how clean and how characterful the spirit is. Cut points are not fixed numbers. They come from tasting and measuring each run. A new distillery needs time and practice to find its own.

We help set up the method, the records and the tasting routine so cut decisions can be repeated and taught.

Maturation is a plan, not a waiting game. Choice of cask, fill strength, warehouse conditions and sampling programme all matter. Warm climates speed up interaction between spirit and wood and also raise evaporation loss, so a warehouse in India behaves differently from one in a cool climate.

Blending, filtering and reducing to bottling strength bring the product together. We support the planning of these steps and the sensory checks behind them.

Quality work includes measuring alcohol strength, testing the spirit for consistency batch to batch and keeping production records that stand up to inspection. Ankur Napa leads on these quality systems and on costing.

In India alcohol is a state subject. Distillery licences, excise control, warehousing rules and label approval vary by state and change. We describe the process and help organise documents, while a licensing adviser or lawyer should guide the application. Always check the current notification.

Engagements start with a review of your plan or plant and a written action plan. We then support the items you choose, remotely by video call and shared data, with site visits by arrangement. The aim is that your team can run the distillery without us.

We do not quote results in advance. If you want to practise the craft before you build, our Craft Distilling and Craft Gin Making courses cover the basics. For planning questions, read common mistakes in project reports, since the same errors appear in distillery plans.
Safety and records from day one

A distillery works with a flammable liquid at high strength, so safety is not a separate topic. It affects room design, electrical fittings and how spirit is stored and moved. It also decides what staff are trained to do in an emergency.

Records matter just as much. Excise authorities expect a clear trail of what went in, what came out and what is in stock. Build the log sheets and stock counting routine before the first run. Fixing missing records afterwards is slow and awkward. It is also the sort of problem inspections find.

We help design simple forms for fermentation, distillation runs and stock movements that fit the way your team works.

Keep the first months modest. Run small batches, taste every run and write down what you changed. A distillery that learns on small volumes makes its expensive mistakes cheaply.

Ask a safety engineer and your local authority to walk the building before commissioning. A second pair of eyes on ventilation and electrics costs little against a fire.
faqs: Which product should a new distillery start with?
That depends on your market, cash and skills. Many start with an unaged spirit to earn while aged spirit matures. Your numbers should decide.
Do you help with trial runs?
Yes. We plan and attend trial runs, remotely or on site, to test the equipment and set cut points before launch.
Can you advise on distilleries outside India?
The science is the same. Licensing and safety rules are local, so use a local adviser for those parts.
